title: Eiffel Tower
blurb: The Eiffel Tower is a 330 m wrought iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, built as the centerpiece of the 1889 Exposition Universelle. It is the most visited monument with an entrance fee in the world.

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: Concrete footings, slabs, compressed-air caissons, and anchor bolts carry the tower to the ground. The north and west legs, closer to the Seine, needed the deepest foundations.

systems.name: Legs
systems.description: Four lattice girders stand apart at the base and come together at the top. They are the primary structure of the tower.

systems.name: Platforms
systems.description: Three visitor levels at 57, 115, and 276 m, carried on iron support girders with railings.

systems.name: Lattice ironwork
systems.description: Cross-braced iron panels join the legs on all four faces, tied by truss rings at each platform level. The finished tower joins 18,038 iron pieces with 2.5 million rivets.

systems.name: Arches
systems.description: Decorative arches spanning between the legs at the base, added by architect Stephen Sauvestre.

systems.name: Elevators
systems.description: Eight elevators serve the tower, running inside the legs to the visitor levels.

systems.name: Stairs
systems.description: Staircases connect the ground to the first and second levels, with over 300 steps per flight.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The summit at 276 m, Gustave Eiffel's apartment, and the broadcasting aerial that brings the tip to 330 m.

explanations.tip beacon: Light assembly at the tip of the antenna. The tower was the tallest structure in the world from 1889 until the Chrysler Building was finished in 1930.

explanations.summit deck: The top visitor platform, 276 m above the ground, the highest public observation deck in the European Union.
